module_title: Union and State Executive & Legislature: Foundational Concepts
introduction: This foundational level introduces the parliamentary system of government in India. It defines the structural separation of powers between the Executive (which implements laws) and the Legislature (which makes laws) at both the Union (Central) and State levels.

core_concepts.title: The Parliamentary System of Government
core_concepts.description:
India follows the Westminster model of parliamentary democracy. 
- Key Feature: There is a strict interdependence between the Executive and the Legislature. The Executive is drawn from the Legislature and is responsible to it.
- Dual Executive: There is a 'Nominal' (De jure/Titular) Executive and a 'Real' (De facto) Executive.

core_concepts.title: The Union Executive (Part V: Articles 52-78)
core_concepts.description:
Consists of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India.
- President: The Nominal Head. All executive actions are taken in their name (Art 53).
- Prime Minister: The Real Head. The PM leads the Council of Ministers (CoM), which aids and advises the President (Art 74).

core_concepts.title: The Union Legislature / Parliament (Part V: Articles 79-122)
core_concepts.description:
Parliament is Bicameral (has two houses). It consists of the President, the Rajya Sabha, and the Lok Sabha.
- Rajya Sabha (Council of States): The Upper House. Represents the states. It is a permanent body (not subject to dissolution). Members have a 6-year term.
- Lok Sabha (House of the People): The Lower House. Represents the people of India. Directly elected for a 5-year term. It can be dissolved by the President.

core_concepts.title: The State Executive & Legislature (Part VI)
core_concepts.description:
The state level mirrors the Union level.
- State Executive: Consists of the Governor (Nominal Head), Chief Minister (Real Head), Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General.
- State Legislature: Most states are Unicameral (only have a Legislative Assembly / Vidhan Sabha). Only 6 states are Bicameral, possessing an Upper House called the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).

important_entities.name: The President is part of the Parliament
important_entities.key_fact: Article 79 explicitly makes the President an integral part of the Legislature.
important_entities.significance: A highly tested fact. Even though the President does not sit in either House and is the head of the Executive, they are an integral part of the Parliament because a bill passed by both Houses cannot become a law without the President's assent.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners often ask to identify the states with a bicameral legislature. Remember, currently, only 6 states have a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad): **Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka**. (Jammu & Kashmir lost it after its reorganization in 2019).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: KUMBAT (Karnataka, UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use 'KUMBAT' to instantly recall the 6 states that have both a Vidhan Sabha and a Vidhan Parishad.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a question asks 'Who is the real executive authority in the Indian Republic?', the answer is **The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers**, not the President.
